chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The one who remembers Allah, Mighty and Majestic, among the oblivious ones is like the fighter among the fleeing ones, and the fighter among the fleeing ones has Paradise.'
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward for remembering Allah when others are heedless?
ai.summary: In Shia scholarship, this metaphor from al-Kafi highlights the concept of 'iqama' (standing firm) in faith during times of spiritual negligence, positioning the dhakir as a solitary defender of divine truth. The comparison to a soldier fighting off retreating troops underscores the active, combative nature of maintaining remembrance against the tide of heedlessness, a theme central to the struggle of the Imams and their followers. This hadith thus elevates dhikr from mere ritual to a vital spiritual defense mechanism with the ultimate reward of Jannah.
